paraphrase: Chapter 16 (Kṛṣṇa to Arjuna; no question opens it). Structure: (1) 16.1–3 the divine endowment (daivī sampad), twenty-six qualities from fearlessness to absence of excessive pride; (2) 16.4 the demonic endowment (āsurī sampad): hypocrisy, arrogance, excessive pride, anger, harshness, ignorance; (3) 16.5 their results — release and bondage — and the assurance to Arjuna that he is born to the divine one ('do not grieve'); (4) 16.6–20 the two creations of beings and a long portrait of the demonic: their not knowing engagement and withdrawal (pravṛtti, nivṛtti) and their lack of purity, conduct and truth (16.7), their view that the world is without truth, foundation or Lord and caused by desire (16.8), their destructive deeds, insatiable desire, anxiety and unjust getting (16.9–12), their boasting inner speech (16.13–15), their fall into hell (16.16), their sacrifices in name only and hatred of the Lord in all bodies (16.17–18), and the Lord's casting them into demonic wombs birth after birth, down to the lowest state (16.19–20); (5) 16.21–22 desire, anger and greed as the threefold gate of hell, freedom from which leads to the highest goal; (6) 16.23–24 whoever sets aside the ordinance of scripture attains neither perfection, happiness nor the highest goal, so scripture is the authority for what is to be done. Purpose, as the chapter presents it: to distinguish the two endowments by their results, reassure Arjuna, and direct him to act by the authority of scripture.

(3) Novelty (apūrvatā), as the text marks it: a lost yoga given again as 'the highest secret' (4.1–3), the 'royal secret' known directly (9.1–2), a form 'not seen before' (11.47–48), 'the most secret teaching' (15.20); at the close a graded mark — 'more secret than the secret' (18.63), then 'hear again my supreme word, the most secret of all' (18.64) — set on 18.65–66. (4) Stated result (phala): peace, the nirvāṇa of brahman and freedom from the bondage of action and of birth, coming to the Lord and the eternal place by his grace (2.39, 2.51, 2.71–72, 4.9, 5.24–26, 8.15–16, 9.34, 14.20, 18.56, 18.62, 18.65–66); and the result shown in the story itself: 'delusion is destroyed, memory regained through your grace; I stand firm, my doubts gone; I will do your word' (18.73). By these marks the Gītā's purport is a teaching that removes Arjuna's grief and his delusion about dharma and brings him to act at Kṛṣṇa's word (2.7–11 → 18.66, 18.72–73), through knowledge of the embodied one who is not slain and does not act (2.19–21, 13.30, 13.32), action done as one's own dharma without attachment to its fruit and offered to the Lord (2.47, 3.30, 9.27–28, 18.46, 18.57), and knowing the Lord and taking refuge in him with devotion (7.14, 11.54, 18.55, 18.62, 18.66), by whose grace the eternal place is reached. The text itself once gives these an order — own work offered as worship, the perfection of freedom from action, the discipline that makes one fit for becoming brahman, supreme devotion, knowing and entering the Lord (18.45–55) — and says that the one who takes refuge in him reaches the eternal place even while acting (18.56); it closes on the word it marks as 'the most secret of all' (18.64): 'be one whose mind is on me, my devotee, one who sacrifices to me; bow to me … abandoning all dharmas, go to me alone for refuge; I will release you from all sins; do not grieve' (18.65–66). The marks do not settle what 'abandoning all dharmas' means, or which of these means is the final and direct one: there the traditions divide.

notes: Written by the merger of the last chunk (role M, Part 7 step 4) from the merged six-marks notes of chs. 1–15 and extractors A and B's notes on chs. 16–18; every mark is cited by this edition's verse numbers (ch. 13 has the extra opening verse). The traditions draw different theses from the same marks — above all the opening 2.11 and the close 18.66 — as recorded in dsp:gita-primary-teaching (positions recalled, not checked against the bhāṣyas; to be checked in Wave 2): Advaita (Śaṅkara; Madhusūdana Sarasvatī): liberation by knowledge of the self alone, steadfastness in knowledge preceded by the renunciation of all works, action done as an offering purifying the mind for it; 18.66 read as renouncing all works, dharma and adharma alike, and resting in the Lord as the self; Madhusūdana's three hexads (action 1–6, devotion 7–12, knowledge 13–18). Viśiṣṭādvaita (Yāmuna's Gītārthasaṅgraha; Rāmānuja): Nārāyaṇa, the supreme brahman, reached by bhakti-yoga, which karma-yoga and jñāna-yoga prepare; 18.66 read as giving up the sense of agency, possession and fruit within all the yogas, or, for one unable to begin bhakti-yoga, as refuge in place of the other means; in the Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition 18.66 is the carama-śloka, the charter of prapatti. Dvaita (Madhva): the supremacy of Viṣṇu and the eternal difference of the selves; liberation by his grace through devotion grounded in knowledge of his supremacy, with desireless action as worship (15.16–18, 18.46). Abhinavagupta (Kashmir Śaiva; low confidence in data/): knowledge and action together — the one established in knowledge acts and is not bound (18.17, 4.18). Bhāskara (Bhedābheda; low confidence): knowledge combined with works (3.20). Gauḍīya (Viśvanātha Cakravartin, Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa): pure devotion to Kṛṣṇa, the most secret teaching (9.34, 18.64–66). Recent (B. G. Tilak): energetic action by the one who knows, for the welfare of the world (5.2, 3.25). The dispute's recorded reconciliation (P3 path, P4 stage, P8 six marks; partially reconciled) claims only that the text addresses different temperaments and stages; which means is final and direct is not yet reconciled. This entry states what the text's own marks point to, in the text's words, and chooses none of these theses. Candidates for the praise principle (P7-arthavāda), flagged by the chunk mergers and not decided: 4.36, 5.2, 6.46, 12.12, 13.24, 13.26, 18.68–71, 18.78. Novelty was weighed two ways in the chs. 1–3 merge: against ordinary knowledge and the ritual view (A) and against the Upaniṣads, which the Gītā often echoes (B: 2.19–20 ≈ Kaṭha 1.2.18–19, 3.42 ≈ Kaṭha 1.3.10, the aśvattha of 15.1 ≈ Kaṭha 2.3.1); the entry cites the text's own marks of novelty, its marks of secrecy. The order of 18.45–55 (devotion after becoming brahman) and the place of 18.56 (refuge while acting: a further stage or a parallel route) are read differently by the traditions (dsp:is-knowledge-the-means-of-bhakti, dsp:bhakti-jnana-precedence).
